_about: Данные для /changelog/. Записи выведены из истории git, но написаны для людей, а не скопированы из заголовков коммитов: пользователю нужно знать, что изменилось в продукте, а не что мы переставляли в репозитории. Сверять с `git log v0.2.7..HEAD -- extension-chrome core`.

releases.note: Not in the store yet. 0.3.0 is still in review.

Fixed: Search no longer piles up expanded branches. Typing a query letter by letter meant every intermediate word — "R" before "Rotterdam" — expanded everything it matched, and none of it collapsed again: a document that should show eighty rows showed a thousand, with the match lost among them.
Search only scrolls when the first match is off screen, instead of tugging the page towards a line that is already in front of you.

releases.note: Not in the store yet. Built from the repository; the site is running this code, the extension build has not been through a manual pass.

Added: Line numbers in the formatted tree, and a setting to switch them off.
A button that jumps straight to the line a parse error is on, and highlights it.
Website, Rate us and Source links in the settings popup.
Sample JSON files at jsonbeautifier.dev/samples/ — an ordinary response, a 2.3 MB one, and one that is deliberately broken.
Changed: Parse errors now read like an editor, not a stack trace: the message, then the line and column, then the offending line with a caret under the exact character. The old text ended in “at position 282”, which nobody can locate by eye.
The raw view shows the source exactly as it arrived. A line too wide for the browser to draw is wrapped, and says so rather than showing an empty screen.
New colours throughout, matching the site.
The settings popup follows the theme you chose in the extension, not only the one your system is set to.
Fixed: The popup showed a white edge along the bottom and right in dark mode.
Clicking the gear while the popup was already open opened the settings page in a separate tab.
Controls that need a parsed document are now dimmed with the reason in a tooltip. Raw is marked as already active instead of simply dead — the source is always there, so “unavailable” was never true.

releases.note: Reviewed and published on the Chrome Web Store.

Added: Automatic formatting: open any raw JSON URL and it is already a tree.
Collapse and expand any branch, with windowed rendering so a multi-megabyte document does not freeze the tab.
Search across the whole document, including branches that have not been rendered yet.
Click a key to copy its JSONPath, click a value to copy the value, or copy the whole document.
Light and dark themes, indent width, auto-expand depth and key sorting.
A visible parse-error view — a document that looks like JSON but does not parse says so instead of showing a blank page.
